engagement_background.objective: Achieve $0.9–$1.7 million in cost savings through a six-month strategic sourcing program that leverages Royal Food Service’s enterprise-wide purchasing power, while maintaining or improving service levels and product quality, delivering quick-hit savings by year-end 2024 and full implementation by March 2025.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Roughly $33.9 million in indirect spend across 15+ categories is in scope, with the top five (Inbound Freight, Non-IT Temporary Labor, Fleet, Fuel, Corrugated) representing 76 % of the baseline. Low-spend/low-opportunity areas may be dropped after initial analysis, and spend may be re-categorized as better data is obtained.
constraints_challenges: Supplier lack of responsiveness to data and usage requests
Potential supplier pushback and risk of unsanctioned 'side conversations', necessitating a unified communication strategy
Limited internal line-item usage data, requiring dependence on supplier-provided information
Key stakeholder availability constraints for data provision, interviews and deliverable reviews
Aggressive timeline for quick-hit savings by end of 2024 and full project completion by March 2025
Incumbent supplier sensitivities during competitive sourcing and negotiations

procurement_environment.data_availability: Basic unit-level spend and invoice data exist internally, but detailed line-item usage often must be requested from suppliers; contracts are available but not centrally organized.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Category definitions and spend baselines require refinement; internal data sometimes lacks granularity, prompting re-categorization and reliance on supplier data to complete baselines.
